answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds each identity to a cryptographic stake burning mechanism where the required burn scales quadratically: attacking N slots costs O(N²). An adversary attempting to harvest consensus rewards faces superlinear cost scaling that outpaces linear payoff. Like trees rooted deeply in an ancient grove, identities draw verifiable security weight from irreversible sacrifice; dark sable thresholds filter ephemeral bots, while any drained capital is routed into an unrecoverable burn lagoon.
